visitors.name: Ducks
visitors.blurb: They found the pond all by themselves.
visitors.hint: They look for open water. A good-sized pond will do.

visitors.name: Hens
visitors.blurb: Busy, opinionated, and very fond of the coop.

visitors.name: The cat
visitors.blurb: Moved in the moment the cottage had a roof.

visitors.name: Butterflies
visitors.blurb: Four flower patches is all it takes.

visitors.name: Bees
visitors.blurb: Humming between the hive and the blooms.
visitors.hint: They'll need a hive to come home to.

visitors.name: Fireflies
visitors.blurb: They only come out when the lamps do.

visitors.name: The owl
visitors.hint: Watches from the pines at night.
visitors.clue: At night: a stump with three pines within two tiles.
visitors.blurb: Sits on the stump like it was carved there. Blinks about once an hour.

visitors.name: The heron
visitors.hint: Fishes where the reeds grow thick.
visitors.clue: At dawn or by day: a pond of twenty tiles and four reeds, each touching two water tiles.
visitors.blurb: Patience on two very long legs.

visitors.name: The hedgehog
visitors.hint: Snuffles about after dark, near shelter and something to eat.
visitors.clue: At dusk or night, outside winter: a log pile with two shrubs and a veggie bed within two tiles.
visitors.blurb: Eats the slugs, ignores the lettuce. The perfect guest.

visitors.name: The fox
visitors.hint: Likes somewhere warm and strawy at the edges of the day.
visitors.clue: At dusk or dawn: a hay bale with three tall grass within three tiles, and eight trees.
visitors.blurb: Curls up on the hay and pretends not to see the hens.

visitors.name: The frog
visitors.hint: Sings where lily pads and reeds meet.
visitors.clue: In spring or summer: two lily pads, each with a reed and another lily pad beside it.
visitors.blurb: Sings for an hour after rain. Nobody asked it to.

visitors.name: The koi
visitors.hint: Something bright moves under a bridge.
visitors.clue: By day: a pond of twenty-four tiles and a footbridge with two lily pads within two tiles.
visitors.blurb: Older than the corner, probably. It isn't telling.

visitors.name: The robin
visitors.hint: Comes when it's cold, to a feeder.
visitors.clue: On winter mornings and days: a bird feeder with two lengths of hedge within two tiles.
visitors.blurb: Follows Laeticia round the beds, hoping she'll dig something up.

visitors.name: The deer
visitors.hint: Steps out of a big wood in the cold seasons.
visitors.clue: In autumn or winter, at dawn or dusk: three apple trees close together, and sixteen trees in all.
visitors.blurb: Takes one apple, very politely, and is gone.

seasons.name: Summer
seasons.line: Summer. Long days and short shadows.

seasons.name: Autumn
seasons.line: Autumn. My favourite. Don't tell the others.

stages.name: The west meadow
stages.line: The brambles are gone. There's a stream back there.

stages.name: The far pond
stages.line: There was a pond back there all along.

stages.name: The old orchard
stages.line: An old orchard. Somebody loved this place once.

stages.name: The high wood
stages.line: Look at that. A whole wood.

wishes.text: It's a bit bare, isn't it? A few more flowers would help. Four patches, say.
wishes.thanks: There. Now it smells like somewhere.

wishes.text: I've slept under the stars two nights running. A cottage would be lovely.
wishes.thanks: A door that closes. A kettle. I'm home.

wishes.text: A path up to the door, so I stop tracking mud inside.
wishes.thanks: Much better. My boots thank you.

wishes.text: The cat keeps sitting right where a bench would go, just by the cottage.
wishes.thanks: The cat has claimed it. Of course.

wishes.text: Three veggie beds, and we'll always have something to cook.
wishes.thanks: Little rows. I do love little rows.

wishes.text: When something in the beds is ripe, pick it and I'll make soup.
wishes.thanks: Soup tonight. I'll leave the pot on.

wishes.text: I'd like to read outside after dark. A lamp beside a bench?
wishes.thanks: Just enough light for one more chapter.

wishes.text: The hens wander off at every chance. A bit of fence round the coop?
wishes.thanks: They're pretending they don't mind.

wishes.text: The ducks would like somewhere to hide. Some tall grass along the water?
wishes.thanks: Three heads, then none. Then three again.

wishes.text: The butterflies slow right down over the lavender. Three patches of it?
wishes.thanks: The bees will hear about this.

wishes.text: The bees fly a long way for flowers. Six near the hive would help.
wishes.thanks: The hum's gone warm and lazy.

wishes.text: A bigger pond, so the ducks have room to argue.
wishes.thanks: They're arguing already. Perfect.

wishes.text: I'd love to get across the water without wading.
wishes.thanks: Dry feet. Small miracles.

wishes.text: The cat has found the warm side of the campfire. Somewhere to sit beside it?
wishes.thanks: Two of us by the fire now. Three, counting the cat.

wishes.text: More trees, of different kinds. A little wood to walk in.
wishes.thanks: Listen to that. Leaves.

wishes.text: A bench under the trees, for listening to the birds.
wishes.thanks: Shade and birdsong. That's my afternoon gone.

wishes.text: Two apple trees side by side would suit something I have in mind.
wishes.thanks: Now. About that something.

wishes.text: The hens watch the veggie beds like it's the theatre. Beds nearer the coop?
wishes.thanks: Front-row seats, and they know it.

wishes.text: A hedge would keep the wind off the garden. Eight lengths, say.
wishes.thanks: Shelter. You can hear the difference.

wishes.text: An arch set into the hedge, like a proper garden gate.
wishes.thanks: I've walked through it four times. Just because.

wishes.text: I'd like to eat lunch looking at the water. A bench by the pond?
wishes.thanks: Bread, cheese and ducks. Lovely.

wishes.text: My trowel keeps going missing. A shed near the beds?
wishes.thanks: Found it. It was in my pocket all along.

wishes.text: With a greenhouse beside the beds, we could grow things through the winter.
wishes.thanks: Speaking of winter, a robin comes to feeders by hedges.

wishes.text: Stack a few hay bales and I'll start dreaming about a barn.
wishes.thanks: It smells like August in there.

wishes.text: A barn and six beds. A windmill would make it a farm.
wishes.thanks: Look at it turn. I could watch it all day.

wishes.text: The ducks keep nosing at the lily pads. A few more would please them no end.
wishes.thanks: Paddling in circles. Pure bliss.

wishes.text: The fireflies glow brightest far from the lamps. A dark patch of long grass?
wishes.thanks: Like the sky came down for a look.

wishes.text: A little square of cobbles, for sitting out. We've no market, but still.
wishes.thanks: There. Now it's a square.

wishes.text: Someone planted an orchard here long ago. Shall we fill the gaps?
wishes.thanks: I found their old wall stones. We can mend it now.

wishes.text: The hens fuss at dusk, as if something's watching. A light by the coop?
wishes.thanks: Calmer now. Whatever it was, it's only curious.

wishes.text: At night the cat stares into the pines. Something lives there. Or could.
wishes.thanks: Whatever it's waiting for, it seems very sure.

wishes.text: The ducks keep to the far side lately, watching the reeds. More reeds?
wishes.thanks: Something tall stood there at dawn. I'm sure of it.

wishes.text: The fireflies love the pond at night. Reeds and lily pads, close together?
wishes.thanks: Someone small went 'plop' just now.

wishes.text: I heard snuffling under the bushes last night. A log pile near them, perhaps?
wishes.thanks: If it comes back, it has somewhere to sleep.

wishes.text: The apples are turning. Plant a few more, and see who comes for them.
wishes.thanks: Leave some on the ground. Just in case.

wishes.text: A big pond with a bridge to lean on. I like watching water from a bridge.
wishes.thanks: Was that orange? Something orange, down deep.

nooks.name: Reading nook
nooks.blurb: A bench, a lamp, and a tree for shade.
nooks.gift: Laeticia reads here in the afternoons.

nooks.name: Lakeside lunch
nooks.teaser: Lunch with a view of the water.
nooks.blurb: A picnic table close enough to hear the ducks.
nooks.gift: After a harvest, Laeticia eats lunch here and the ducks drift over.

nooks.name: Kitchen garden
nooks.teaser: Beds, and someone to guard them.
nooks.blurb: Four beds and a scarecrow keeping an eye on them.
nooks.gift: Beds here grow a little faster, and the hens come to peck.

nooks.name: Firefly hollow
nooks.teaser: Long grass, mushrooms, and no lamps.
nooks.blurb: A dark, damp, grassy place the fireflies adore.
nooks.gift: Fireflies gather here, and more of them come.

nooks.name: Hen yard
nooks.teaser: A fenced yard with hay to scratch in.
nooks.blurb: A coop, a fence, and hay to scratch about in.
nooks.gift: The hens spend their afternoons here.

nooks.name: Duck cove
nooks.teaser: Lily pads, reeds, and room to swim.
nooks.blurb: A sheltered bit of pond with lilies and reeds.
nooks.gift: The ducks sleep on this bank at night.

nooks.name: Bee garden
nooks.teaser: A hive in a garden of many flowers.
nooks.blurb: Lavender, sunflowers, and a hive in the middle of it all.
nooks.gift: Two more bees join the hive.

nooks.name: Orchard
nooks.blurb: Five apple trees, close enough to share their bees.
nooks.gift: Apples fall in autumn, and the deer come sooner.

nooks.name: Village square
nooks.teaser: Cobbles, a fountain, a seat and a lamp.
nooks.blurb: A fountain on cobbles, with a seat and a lamp.
nooks.gift: Laeticia sketches here on fine afternoons.

nooks.name: Campfire circle
nooks.teaser: A fire with seats and wood to burn.
nooks.blurb: Two seats, a fire, and a pile of logs to keep it going.
nooks.gift: Laeticia and the cat sit here together at dusk.

nooks.name: Secret garden
nooks.teaser: Behind a hedge, through an arch.
nooks.blurb: Hedges all round, flowers inside, and a bench to hide on.

nooks.name: Little harbour
nooks.teaser: A boat, a way across, and a light.
nooks.blurb: A rowing boat tied up by a lamp and a crossing.
nooks.gift: The heron fishes here, and the ducks paddle past.

nooks.name: Woodland walk
nooks.blurb: A path under the branches, mushrooms along the edge.
nooks.gift: Laeticia takes her evening stroll here, and leaves fall thicker.

nooks.name: Farmyard
nooks.teaser: Barn, coop, hay and beds together.
nooks.blurb: A barn with hens, hay and beds around it.
nooks.gift: The cat naps on the hay.

nooks.name: Moon garden
nooks.blurb: Daisies that glow in the lamplight, and a bench to see them from.
nooks.gift: Laeticia steps out at night to see it.

nooks.name: Wishing well
nooks.teaser: A well on cobbles, among flowers.
nooks.blurb: A well with cobbles round it and flowers at its feet.
nooks.gift: Laeticia tosses in a pebble when she passes.

resident.name: Laeticia
resident.blurb: Drew other people's gardens for forty years. This one is hers.

tour: Oh, it's lovely. A bit bare, though.
greet: Oh good, I was hoping you'd come by.
morning: Another day. Let's see what's grown.
Up with the birds, as usual.
Cold dew, warm tea. Good morning.
dusk: The sky's doing its show again.
One more cup of tea, then bed.
no_cottage_night: Stars again. They are very nice stars.
The ground's harder than I remember.
Someday, a roof. Tonight, a blanket.
home_lost: Well. Back to the stars, then.
I'll find somewhere to sleep. Somehow.
rain_start: Rain. The beds will be pleased.
I'll be inside if anyone wants me.
snow_start: Snow. I'll put the kettle on.
Look at it come down. Not a sound.
wish_offer: Just an idea. No hurry at all.
I've been meaning to say something.
already_done: Well, look at that. It's already there.
place_flower: The bees will find that by lunch.
I'll press one for the sketchbook.
place_tree: Something to sit under in fifty years.
Good spot. It'll like the light there.
place_water: I do like the sound of water.
place_home: A whole building. Look at you.
I'll have a peek inside later.
place_light: Good. I'm forever tripping over things.
place_seat: Somewhere to sit. My favourite thing.
place_stone: I do like a good rock.
place_other: I wouldn't have thought of that.
harvest_ready: Something's ripe, if you want to pick it.
The beds are ready when you are.
harvest_done: I'll take that in. Thank you.
nook_found: Oh, that's a proper little spot.
That deserves a name. Let me think.
click: Did you know daisies close at night?
Forty years drawing other people's gardens.
I'm not old. I'm well watered.
idle: I talk to the plants. They don't mind.
Hm. That corner wants a little something.
The light here is good for drawing.
I wonder who lived here before.
Quiet. Just how I like it.
I could sit here all afternoon.
first_duck: Ducks already. They don't waste time.
first_hen: Hens. Opinionated ones, by the look.
first_cat: Well. I suppose we have a cat now.
first_butterfly: A butterfly. Hold still, I'll draw it.
first_bee: Bees. Mind the hive, it's their house.
first_firefly: Fireflies. I haven't seen those in years.
first_owl: An owl. Don't stare, you'll make it shy.
first_heron: A heron. Stand still and it might stay.
first_fox: A fox. It's only curious. I think.
first_frog: Someone's singing in the lily pads.
first_koi: Something orange in the deep water.
first_robin: A robin. It thinks it owns the place.
